proiect-de-grup.text: In a group project, nobody has taken their part yet. Which one do you take?
options: I make the plan: who does what, and by when
I do the calculations, tables and charts
I write the text and present it to the class
I do the visual part: design, images, video
I build the model or the app

prieten-stresat.text: Someone close to you is very stressed before an exam. What do you do?
options: I listen and try to calm things down
I explain the lessons they haven't understood
I suggest a walk or a game so they can let off steam
I make a study schedule, by days and hours
I explain what happens in the body under stress and how to calm it down

peste-zece-ani.text: In ten years, what would you like people to say about your work?
options: It improved the lives of many people who were sick or in need
It discovered something new about how the world works
It changed a law, or the way a community is run, for the better
It created something people remember
It started a business and made it grow

zi-de-lucru.text: Which working day would suit you best?
options: A clear schedule, precise rules, everything in its place
Every day different, always on the move, out in the field
Quiet and focus, with a hard problem to solve
Always among people: students, customers, patients
Freedom: I choose my own projects and my own pace

atelier-gratuit.text: You have a free day and a free workshop at school. Which one do you pick?
options: Electronics: you build a circuit that really works
First aid: you learn what to do until the ambulance arrives
Debating: you defend an opinion in front of a jury
Photography or film: you tell a story through pictures
Nature exploration: you recognise plants, animals and tracks

canalul-scolii.text: The school is launching an online channel run by students. What role would you like?
options: Writer: I write articles and interviews
Field reporter: I cover the matches, trips and events
Video editor or graphic designer
The one who builds the website and fixes the technical problems
The one who finds sponsors and manages the budget

job-de-vara.text: You can work one summer in one of these places. Which appeals to you most?
options: A vet's practice or a care centre for the elderly
A building site, a farm or bike courier work
A shop: you advise customers on what to buy
A weather station or a laboratory: you measure and record
A summer camp: you are an activity leader for children

internet-picat.text: The internet goes down in your whole building. What do you do?
options: I check the cables and the router and try one thing after another
I note what changed today and rule out the causes one by one
I ask the neighbours if they have the same problem and we call the provider together
I write a clear complaint and ask for what I am entitled to

specie-pe-cale-de-disparitie.text: You find out that a species in the lake near your town is disappearing. What do you do?
options: I want to understand the causes: water samples, observations
I gather volunteers and organise an action
I run a campaign: a poster, a clip, a story that catches on
I ask for stricter rules through a petition
I go and clean the shore with my own hands

ce-te-motiveaza.text: What would keep you going with an activity, even after months?
options: I see myself improving: times, scores, records
I help someone make progress
I keep learning new things about how the world works
I get responsibility and things go well because of me
I can do things my own, original way

documentar.text: You have a free hour. Which documentary would you choose?
options: How a bridge, an aeroplane or a satellite is built
How an empire fell or how a country changed
How the cell, the brain or the universe works
How doctors and nurses work in an emergency hospital
How a small company grew into a well-known one

sanatate-in-scoala.text: You are asked to do something for the health of the students in your school. Where do you start?
options: I find out what problems students have: conversations and a short survey
I organise active breaks and a sports tournament
I give talks about sleep and nutrition, with checked information
I write a clear letter to the head teacher, with arguments and proposals
I work out the cost and look for who could fund us

doua-ore-fara-plictiseala.text: Which of these activities could you do for two hours without getting bored?
options: Sorting data in a table and finding what repeats
Repairing or assembling something from parts
Explaining something to someone until they understand
Sketching or composing something from scratch
Reading about a problem in society and forming an opinion

unde-lucrezi.text: Where would you like to spend most of your working time?
options: Outdoors: in a field, in a forest, on a building site or on a sports ground
In a hospital or a clinic, next to people who need help
In an office with a team: discussions, plans, meetings
In a workshop or a laboratory, with equipment
In a studio or a newsroom, where something is being created

cearta-in-echipa.text: Two teammates are arguing and the project is stuck. What do you do?
options: I listen to both and look for a solution they can agree on
I suggest clear rules and divide the tasks differently
I put the facts on the table: who said what, what happened
I suggest a break with some movement so everyone can relax
I tell each of them how the situation looks from the other's side

regula-nedreapta.text: The student council votes for a rule that is unfair to some of your classmates. What do you do?
options: I read the regulations and the students' rights, then I challenge it
I run a survey and bring figures that show the effects
I tell real cases so everyone understands what it means
I bring together the people affected and we talk it through
I quickly set up an online petition with a simple website

mandru-de-tine.text: At the end of the year, which of these would make you happiest?
options: I finished something hard with my own hands: I repaired or built it
I helped a person or an animal in need
I improved at a sport through steady training
I understood something complicated about nature or science
I convinced people and organised something big

problema-de-cartier.text: There is a problem in your neighbourhood that bothers everyone (rubbish, a damaged road, a run-down playground). What role do you take?
options: I collect signatures and go to the town hall to ask for a fix
I work out what it would cost and what can be done with little money
I roll up my sleeves and we fix together what can be fixed
I find the causes: what pollutes, what breaks and why
I write a post or a letter that people will read
